item.title: Raul Pereda of Jacksonville takes another step in returning to the PGA Tour
item.description: Raul Pereda, who is scrambling to regain the PGA Tour card he earned at the 2023 Q School, advanced to second-stage qualifying with a tie for ninth Oct. 27-30 at the Sand Creek Station Golf Club in Newtown, Kan. Pereda, a native of Mexico who has lived in Jacksonville since he was 14 and then played for the Jacksonville University Dolphins, shot 67 in the first round and easily cleared the number to advance with an 11-under 277. The top-18 players, plus ties who shot 6-under or lower, will play in one of five second-stage qualifiers Dec. 1-4. The next step after that is the PGA Tour Q School , presented by Korn Ferry, Dec. 10-13 at the TPC Sawgrass Dye's Valley and the Sawgrass Country Club. Two other Jacksonville residents, former Ohio State golfer Jackson Chandler and former Elon golfer Matthew Doyle, also qualified for second stage. Chandler tied for sixth at The Preserve at Iron Horse in West Palm Beach at 13-under 275, with closing rounds of 66-68, and Doyle tied for 11th at the Abilene (Texas) Country Club at 13-under 275, with a 66 in the final round. Other area residents who previously advanced from first-stage qualifying are former University of North Florida players Brandon Mancheno and Robbie Higgins, former Florida Gator Tyson Alexander, Sam Nicholson and Carl Yuan. item.title: Former F1 champion Jones dies aged 80
item.description: Jones helped turn Williams into one of the major forces in F1 [Getty Images] Alan Jones, the last Australian and first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world title, has died at the age of 80. Jones raced in F1 between 1975 and 1986, winning the title in 1980 to become the first of Williams' seven world champions. Jones, who turned 80 on Monday, won 12 grands prix in his career and raced competitively in other formats until 2002. "We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released on her behalf by Motorsport Australia. "He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for." Jones started the first of his 116 F1 races in a Hesketh at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix. He won his first race for the Shadow team in Austria in 1977 before joining Williams the following year. After finishing third in the drivers' championship in 1979, he won five races in 1980 and finished on the podium in all but one of the grands prix he completed, taking the title ahead of Nelson Piquet. Jones was the second Australian to win the F1 championship, after Jack Brabham in 1959, 1960 and 1966. Jones remains the most recent Australian to triumph at the Australian Grand Prix, winning at Melbourne's Calder Park Raceway in 1980 when the race was not part of the world championship. He finished third in the drivers' standings in 1981, winning in Las Vegas for what proved to be his final race victory. He retired at the end of the season. Having appeared in one race for Arrows in 1983, Jones made a full-time comeback with new team Haas in 1985 and raced largely unsuccessfully the following year. He continued to compete in touring car and endurance races, mostly in Australia, and became a popular motorsports pundit on television in his home country. "Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way," Butler-Davis said. "Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe." Breaking new ground with Williams Jones, the Williams FW07 and Patrick Head and Frank Williams in Brazil in 1981 [Getty Images] Alan Jones' time at the very peak of F1 was short - essentially just under three years from mid-1979 to the end of 1981 - but he left a lasting impression. Jones is synonymous with the Williams team, having become their first world champion in 1980, and he formed a close, almost brotherly bond with co-founders Frank Williams and Patrick Head. Williams and Head loved Jones' pugnacious, no-nonsense approach, and between them they were the leading force in F1 for a short time, as the team first emerged at the forefront of the sport. item.title: One year after 'Let it Rip' meeting, Trevor Lawrence has elevated game
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars were a surprising 4-3, but his quarterback was still searching to sync his in-week preparation and game-day production when Liam Coen welcomed Trevor Lawrence into his second-floor office on Oct. 20, 2025. Lawrence was a tireless worker who made the right pre-snap decisions but was plagued by bouts of indecisiveness. Before sending him on his bye week, Coen showed Lawrence multiple examples in which the play was right there had he pulled the trigger. “I just have to trust it,” Lawrence told Coen. The summit could eventually be remembered as one of the most important meetings — The "Let It Rip" meeting — in Jaguars history. The coach showed confidence and belief in his franchise quarterback but also urged him to be more aggressive. In the 17 regular season games since, the Jaguars are 14-3 and Lawrence has totals of 37 touchdowns, 11 interceptions, 4,669 passing yards, a 63.9 completion rate and a 109.9 passer rating. High-level stuff. MVP stuff. Winning stuff. A player who used to tease with bits of elite play is now one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. He enters the Jaguars’ Nov. 5 game at the Baltimore Ravens with a league-best 112.6 passer rating; he started the season with a career 86.3 rating. The Jaguars are 5-2 thanks in part to Lawrence’s level-jump — check that, multi-level jump. Just as the Chicago Bears have been reborn with the Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, so have the Jaguars with Coen and Lawrence. Admit it: For the first time since maybe 1999, you, the Jaguars fan, expects your team to win every week and when they don’t, there is a sky-is-falling reaction. Feels good, doesn’t it? It sure does within Jaguars headquarters, where the collaboration between Coen and Lawrence has advanced to the pro football equivalent of Ph.D. courses. “Very far,” Coen told The Times-Union on Oct. 20 of Lawrence's progress. “I’m very, very pleased with how he’s seeing things.” What is it like to be around Coen and Lawrence in the quarterback meeting room, when class is in session and plays are tossed out, added or revised? Over the last two weeks, the Times-Union tried to find out. Coen-Lawrence talks have ‘evolved’ So, you’re Joey Aguilar , an undrafted rookie who two years ago was playing at Appalachian State or you’re Quinn Ewers , a second-year player who two years ago was playing at Texas and was traded to the Jaguars on Aug. 29. item.title: Jeremiah Smith is 164 yards from another Big Ten record
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes in action against the USC Trojans during the second quarter at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Lost in the frustration of Ohio State’s 30-18 loss at USC was another piece of history from Jeremiah Smith. With just over two minutes left, Luke Fahey found him for a one yard touchdown. It was the 40th touchdown catch of Smith’s career, breaking Braylon Edwards’ Big Ten record of 39, which had stood since 2004. It didn’t feel like much of a celebration in the moment, but it’s worth remembering just how fast Smith is rewriting the record books. Smith already owns every major receiving record at Ohio State, and now he holds the Big Ten’s career touchdown mark too. The next record could fall this Saturday. The yardage record is within reach Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards at USC, giving him 3,625 career receiving yards. The Big Ten record belongs to Purdue’s John Standeford, who finished with 3,788 yards from 2000 to 2003. That puts Smith 163 yards from tying the record and 164 from breaking it. That’s a big number for most receivers. For Smith, it’s an ordinary afternoon. He had 151 yards against Ball State, 164 at Texas, 217 against Illinois and 206 at Iowa. He’s averaging over 130 receiving yards per game this season, with 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games. When I wrote about the Big Ten record chase in early October, I predicted JJ would break this one at USC on Halloween. Sayin’s injury, a quiet day at Indiana and USC’s game plan pushed it back a week. The timing might work out even better. Breaking it at home against Oregon, in front of the Ohio Stadium crowd, would be a pretty fitting way to do it. Can he get there with Fahey? That’s the real question. Smith’s production has dipped over the last two games. Against Indiana, he had a season-low 68 yards against a defense that threw extra bodies at him on almost every snap. At USC, with Fahey making his first start, he caught 10 passes but averaged just 8.3 yards per catch as Ohio State leaned on quick, short throws. That makes sense. Fahey needed easy completions, and Smith is the most reliable target on the field. But it also means the big plays haven’t been there. To get 164 yards against Oregon, Smith will probably need at least one or two explosive plays down the field. I think there’s reason to believe those will come. Fahey now has a full game under his belt and another week of practice as the starter. Smith said after Indiana that it would, “take time” to build the same chemistry with a new quarterback, but he’s already Fahey’s top target. Smith also caught the record breaking touchdown at USC, which tells you Fahey is looking for him when it matters most. The more reps those two get together, the more comfortable Fahey should be giving Smith a chance to make a play down the field.

item.title: Marco Rose embraces Premier League life and jokes about Thomas Tuchel
item.description: Marco Rose embraces Premier League life and jokes about Thomas Tuchel Former Bundesliga coach Marco Rose has spoken enthusiastically about his first months in English football. The 50-year-old, who previously coached Borussia Mönchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund, and RB Leipzig, is currently enjoying an upturn in fortunes with AFC Bournemouth following a difficult start to the Premier League campaign. After failing to win any of their opening six league fixtures, Bournemouth have recently registered three consecutive victories. Rose’s side have also enjoyed success in European competition, with the German trainer preparing for Thursday’s Europa League encounter against Sparta Prague. Speaking in an interview with Kicker , Rose reflected on his experience in the Premier League and the differences between German and English football. “It’s something special to be able to work there,” Rose explained. “One senses the global attention. It’s football in its purest form. I appreciate German fan culture, but I also like the English version. It’s a little quieter here at times, but when the match calls for it, the stadiums generate extraordinary energy. I like the people in England, who treat one another with great respect. I really feel comfortable here.” Marco Rose jokes about Thomas Tuchel and Marcus Tavernier Rose also reserved praise for Bournemouth attacker Marcus Tavernier, who has scored five goals in nine Premier League appearances this season. Asked whether the 26-year-old might soon receive a call-up from England national team coach Thomas Tuchel, Rose declined to speculate but acknowledged his player’s impressive performances. “You’ll have to ask Thomas about that,” Rose remarked. “But I think several of our lads have made a good case for themselves, and Marcus in particular gives us a great deal.” When asked whether Tuchel had attended a Bournemouth home fixture to watch Tavernier, Rose delivered a lighthearted response. “No, I don’t think so,” Rose said with a laugh. “Perhaps he couldn’t get a ticket because our stadium is a little smaller.” GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: Three Important Questions for Dodgers Before 2027
item.description: Oct 3, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) looks on from the mound after giving up a solo home run to Atlanta Braves catcher Sean Murphy (12) in game one of the NLDS of the 2026 MLB … | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Last season ended in disappointment for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Now, they must assess themselves as they prepare for the future. Here are three questions they must ask if they want to continue their prolonged success into 2027 and beyond. In the Market for Pitching Again? Los Angeles knows better than most that one can never have enough pitching. To that end, they traded for Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline this year. Now, are they willing to keep him? The left-hander is expected to earn a pretty penny this year. Moreover, he has Scott Boras as his agent and an abbreviated window with which to negotiate as December 1 approaches. Los Angeles and President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman have plenty of money at their disposal, provided that their owner doesn’t sell the team. Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches during the first inning of their National League Championship Series game against the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Oct 11, 2026. However, Los Angeles, with a few notable exceptions, is very hesitant to dole out long-term contracts to a player entering free agency who is entering his third decade. The more likely option for a mutual agreement would be a shorter deal in length with a higher AAV, similar to the Kyle Tucker deal. It is said that Los Angeles has some competition for the left-hander’s services; the New York Mets and Chicago Cubs are also interested. Skubal did seem to like it in Los Angeles, but it’s still a question where he will end up. However, those in the know expect a deal signed by December 1. The Youth Movement? Los Angeles has the oldest roster in baseball, and it showed during the National League Championship Series against the World Champion Milwaukee Brewers. The question is how young will the Dodgers go without compromising the veteran core? There is no question that there will be some turnover on the margins. Enrique and Teoscar Hernandez will probably be on different teams in 2027. Josue DePaula will probably cement his place on the roster. Do they sign or trade for a shortstop like Elly de La Cruz ? Will they move Mookie Betts to second base to preserve him from wear and tear on his body? Friedman, in his year-end press conference, addressed the age of the players, but he didn’t seem overly concerned right now. He pointed out that whoever they place on the roster must be major-league ready and fit the team’s needs. It will be interesting to see the evolution of the roster as the offseason progresses. item.title: Report: Mets Hire A.J. Ellis To Major-League Coaching Staff
item.description: Jul 31, 2018; San Diego, CA, USA; San Diego Padres catcher A.J. Ellis looks on during the tenth inning against the San Francisco Giants at Petco Park. Mandatory Credit: Orlando Ramirez-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The New York Mets are hiring A.J. Ellis as their major-league strategy coordinator, The Athletic’s Will Sammon reported Wednesday. The club has not yet announced the move. Ellis becomes the latest addition to manager Andy Green’s coaching staff as the Mets continue preparing for the 2027 season. His arrival also reunites Green with a familiar face from his time managing the San Diego Padres. Mets Hiring A.J. Ellis to Major-League Coaching Staff Ellis, 45, played 11 major-league seasons, most notably with the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also spent time with the Philadelphia Phillies and Miami Marlins before finishing his playing career with San Diego in 2018. Across 672 career games, Ellis hit .239 with 44 home runs and 229 RBI. While his offensive numbers were modest, his experience behind the plate gave him years of working closely with pitchers and handling major-league pitching staffs. Following his retirement, Ellis joined the Padres’ front office as a special assistant in 2019. He now brings both playing and front-office experience to his new role in New York. During his final season as a player, Ellis played under Green in San Diego. That existing relationship could help ease his transition to the Mets, giving him familiarity with the manager as he joins a different organization. Ellis also gained experience mentoring younger players late in his career, helping Padres catchers Austin Hedges and Francisco Mejía in 2018. That background could prove valuable as he establishes relationships with players in New York. The Last Word With one coaching vacancy remaining — after this move becomes official and the promotion of Mariano Duncan — the staff is moving closer to completion. Ellis’ addition gives Green another experienced voice as the Mets look to turn their offseason preparations into better results in 2027. item.description: Sep 1, 2026; Anaheim, California, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) hits a solo home run against the Los Angeles Angels during the first inning at Angel Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Major League Baseball deadline to extend qualifying offers to players was Monday, November 2, at 5 p.m. A qualifying offer is a one-year offer extended by a team to a player who spent the entire previous year with the team-a player can only receive a qualifying offer once. The Yankees had two qualifying offer-eligible players: David Bednar and Jazz Chisholm Jr. While the Yankees extended an offer to Bednar worth $23.15 million, they did not extend one to Chisholm Jr. Why exactly is that, and where do the Yankees go at second base? Where do the Yankees Turn to at Second Base? For starters, Bednar is one of the best closers in baseball. He recorded the third most saves in the American League with 35 this season while posting a 2.47 ERA. After getting traded to the Yankees from Pittsburgh at the 2025 trade deadline, he’s gone 45/52 in save opportunities. He was well deserving of his qualifying offer. Chisholm Jr., on the other hand, had a down season by his standards. He had the worst batting average for a full season at .231 with 19 home runs, a below-league-average OPS at .711 and a 1.7 WAR. However, more positively, he recorded 15 outs above average and stole 41 bases. This is a big slip from his 2025 season, where Chisholm Jr. batted .242 with 31 home runs, 31 stolen bases, a .831 OPS, and a 4.1 WAR. item.title: Frank Bruno names the biggest puncher he ever faced
item.description: When you talk to any boxing fan, especially a British boxing fan, they will likely have plenty of positives to say about former WBC heavyweight champion Frank Bruno. The London-born fighter was beloved by the British public and considered a man of the people. He faced some of the best fighters of his generation, and when appearing on the Fight Your Corner podcast with Tony Bellew and Charlie Parsons , Bruno revealed the five biggest punchers he faced, including who hit harder than Mike Tyson . Frank Bruno ranks five biggest punchers he faced When asked on the Fight Your Corner podcast to rank the five biggest punchers he’s faced, Frank Bruno said: “Bone Crusher Smith was a hard puncher. I would say Tim Witherspoon (hardest puncher).” “He was a dangerous puncher. Very slick, knows his business,” added Bruno. When asked if James “Bone Crusher” Smith was second, Bruno said: “Yeah, definitely.” Revealing the third-biggest puncher, the former WBC champ said: “Mike Tyson at his peak.” Bellew asked Bruno if Tyson was the most ruthless, and he said: “Most definitely, when he’s on his game.” Discussing who would be fourth and fifth out of Oliver McCall and Lennox Lewis: “Oliver McCall. He’s mad. Something’s not right. Very strong guy,” said the Brit. Those selections left Lewis in position five, revealing the five biggest punchers that Bruno ever faced. Frank Bruno Personal Instagram @frankbrunoboxer The Big Fight Weekend verdict Growing up in the era when Frank Bruno (40-5, 38 KOs) was fighting, he was loved by the British public; there is no doubt. My Mum actually met Frank Bruno once and described him as a gentleman after they met at Notting Hill Market back in the 90s. Outside the ring, he was a gentle giant with fans he met. Inside the ring, he mixed with the best, losing twice to Mike Tyson and once to Tim Witherspoon, Lennox Lewis, and James “Bone Crusher Smith.” He memorably went through the trenches to outpoint Oliver McCall to win the WBC title by unanimous decision, with scorecards 115-113 and 117-111 x2. Bruno has gone through his own mental health battles since retiring, but he remains a loved cultural figure in the UK. He may not have been the greatest technical fighter, but he was the most loved. item.title: Sports owners bet big on Republicans. What does their defeat mean for US sports?
item.description: New York governor Kathy Hochul backed public funding for the Buffalo Bills’ stadium, illustrating why Democratic victories don’t necessarily threaten the subsidies sports owners enjoy. Photograph: Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images Before a single vote was cast this election cycle, the technocrats and oligarchs who own American sports had already voted. Pro sports owners put more than $100m into this cycle, according to Front Office Sports. But Tuesday night was a referendum not just on Donald Trump and Maga policies, but on the puppeteers who pull America’s strings. The people voted, and the owners lost. Before anyone frames this as a rescue, a word about the rescuers. Democrats are the instrument for ending Maga, and they are also the other face of the same coin. Think Republicans are behind all of our ills? Think again. New Jersey’s governor, Phil Murphy, placed his state’s first legal sports bet in 2018. Illinois governor JB Pritzker signed sports betting into law a year later. New York’s mobile sportsbooks went live under Governor Kathy Hochul in 2022, with the state taking 51% of the revenue. Pritzker and Hochul both won Tuesday, and all of them are Democrats. In some of the biggest betting markets in the country, the bookmakers’ most reliable partner has been a Democratic statehouse. Having said all that, the biggest losers on Tuesday night were Republicans: Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress. That would have made plenty of sports owners disappointed, as they have a habit of backing Republicans. At least 10 sports owners backed Mike Rogers in Michigan, and Abdul El-Sayed beat Rogers . Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones gave $1m to Trump’s super Pac and $250,000 to a committee backing Ken Paxton, and James Talarico beat Paxton in Texas. The former Mavericks owner Miriam Adelson lapped everyone with at least $67m to Republican committees, in keeping with her history of big spending around elections. What did she get for her money? A House and Senate minority. So how does all this affect the future of American sports? Let’s count the ways. The league’s brief makes two arguments: prediction markets are gambling that belongs under state regulation like any sportsbook, and the money is enormous. item.title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s latest NFL exit raises fresh questions about his career
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been released by the Buffalo Bills after just six games, with NFL Network reporter Cameron Wolfe questioning whether the safety will get another opportunity in the league. The 28-year-old has now played for six different franchises in five years, with concerns over his consistency and disciplinary record following him into another departure. Gardner-Johnson was suspended for one game after spitting towards Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers during their Week 6 meeting. His release came shortly after that suspension ended. Cameron Wolfe questions whether C.J. Gardner-Johnson will get another NFL chance Speaking on NFL The Insiders , Wolfe suggested Gardner-Johnson’s playmaking ability was no longer enough to outweigh the issues surrounding his performances. “His playmaking ability no longer made up for some of the lapses he had. And you combine that with him getting suspended for spitting on a player, it just was not worth it anymore for this Bills team. So they made the decision to move on. And for C.J. Gardner-Johnson, this is the sixth team in the last five years that he’s played on. “I don’t know if he gets to a seventh. It’s been a constant for him in this type of storyline. For the Bills’ defense, they came off their best game of the season without C.J., with Damar Hamlin starting there.” Wolfe also reported that Buffalo had concerns about Gardner-Johnson’s reliability on the field, suggesting his performances had frustrated the coaching staff. Gardner-Johnson started all six games he played for the Bills, recording 26 tackles, two pass breakups and one interception. However, Damar Hamlin stepped into the starting role against the Baltimore Ravens and recorded five tackles and a pass breakup in Buffalo’s 36-10 victory. The safety’s career has included spells with the New Orleans Saints, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions, Houston Texans and Chicago Bears, as well as a brief stint on the Ravens’ practice squad. He also won Super Bowl LIX with Philadelphia after returning to the Eagles in 2024. Gardner-Johnson still has 21 career interceptions across 93 regular-season games, but his latest release leaves his NFL future uncertain. Another team would need to believe his ability to create turnovers outweighs the concerns that have followed him between franchises. item.title: Arizona Cardinals designate Isaiah Adams to return from injured reserve
item.description: It has been a rough season with injuries once again for the Arizona Cardinals, but they could be getting at least one piece back. The team announced they have opened the 21 day practice window for Isaiah Adams, and the Cardinals desperately need help along the offensive line. From the team: The Arizona Cardinals Football Club today announced that the team has designated offensive lineman Isaiah Adams to return from the injured reserve list. Adams can begin practicing and the team can activate him to the 53-man roster at any time during the next 21 days or at the conclusion of the three-week period. In addition, the team has signed running back Jermar Jefferson and wide receiver James Proche II to the practice squad. The signings took place today at the Dignity Health Arizona Cardinals Training Center in Tempe, AZ. Jefferson (5-10, 215) returns to the Cardinals after he played two games with the team last season in addition to spending time on Arizona’s practice squad. In his career, Jefferson has appeared in 11 games (one start) with the Cardinals and Lions and has 96 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries to go along with five receptions for 33 yards. He entered the league with Detroit as a seventh-round pick (257 th overall) in the 2021 NFL Draft out of Oregon State. Proche (5-11, 193) is a seven-year NFL veteran who has played 71 games (three starts) in his career with Tennessee (2025), Cleveland (2023-24) and Baltimore (2020-22). In his career, he has 34 receptions for 364 yards to go along with 68 punt returns for 591 yards (8.7-yard avg.) and four kick returns for 60 yards. Proche entered the league with Baltimore as a sixth-round pick (201 st overall) in the 2020 NFL Draft from SMU. He was on the Browns practice squad earlier this season. Jefferson will wear jersey #37 and Proche will wear #18. The wide receiver position is obviously one of need as well, so the Arizona Cardinals added a couple of pieces there as well, but Adams is really the one to watch, and hopefully he can make it back on the field in the window.

item.title: Napoli Tipped to Go Scorched Earth in January
item.description: Napoli Tipped to Go Scorched Earth in January Napoli suffered another costly loss against Porto in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, complicating their path to qualification. They have been defeated in half of their matches so far this season. Director Giovanni Manna confirmed that they’ll be busy in January but not necessarily in every position, talking to Sky . “The only role where we are set is the attack. Our reflections are constant. We are surely working to do something, but we’ll see where we will be then. We’ll do what needs to be done, but always respecting our parameters.” According to Radio Kiss Kiss , Napoli are setting up a profound overhaul after doing the bare minimum in the summer. They are plotting four acquisitions and four exits. They have too many wingers and too many center-backs, while they are short-handed in the midfield. Massimiliano Allegri considers Kevin De Bruyne a ‘regista’ and wants to add physicality, as Frank Anguissa and Scott McTominay no longer suffice. If they execute their plan, it could lead to the departure of Stanislav Lobotka, who would no longer be central. They could bring in up to three new players in the role, possibly two youngsters. Then, they’ll try to replicate the same model at the end of the season. Our Take on Napoli They surely have to do something significant, as their season is starting to go down the drain already. They might be the first team to buck the trend if the rumored strategy sees the light of day, massively changing the squad rather than the coach. Their flaws were evident in the summer already, when they were bafflingly quiet, and then a slew of injuries exacerbated them. Doing business in January generally comes at a higher cost.

item.description: Chelsea star puts Xabi Alonso under pressure for big decision this weekend Emi Martinez is keen to face Sunderland this weekend, but the decision will come down to Xabi Alonso when hep picks his team. He says that Martinez has been “pushing” to play in Sunday’s game against Sunderland, in part because he wants to prove his fitness for his country during hte upcoming international break. item.title: Lakers offense stumbles, defense carries in 116-103 win over Sacramento
item.description: Sacramento Kings forward/center Domantas Sabonis (11) puts up a shot against Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) during the first quarter at Golden 1 Center. SACRAMENTO, Calif. –– There is a particular silence that falls over a basketball team when the offense goes cold — a silence that lives in the spaces between possessions, in the clank of a rim rejecting what the scouting report predicted, in the way players start pressing, forcing, trying to generate with force what won't come with flow. It is the silence of a band that lost its drummer mid-set. Everybody still has the sheet music. Nobody has the time. Wednesday night in Sacramento, the Lakers lived in that silence for long stretches. Their shots were short, their threes wouldn't drop, their free-flowing, league-leading offense — 122 offensive rating, 52% shooting, the best in the NBA coming in — played like it was stuck in mud. Fouls stopped the clock. Timeouts broke the flow. The game got choppy, ugly and weird. And the Lakers won by 13 –– comfortably. That's the story of this 116-103 victory over the Kings, and it's the most encouraging kind of story a 7-2 team can tell about itself: on a night the music died, somebody else picked up the instrument. What Luka Dončić is doing right now defies logic. His 40 points, nine rebounds and seven assists led all scorers. Dončić rained in six made threes, for his third consecutive 40-point game, his fourth in his last five, his 67th career game at 40 or better. His sixth straight game scoring at least 35. And — this is the part that makes historians lean forward — 308 total points through his first eight games of the season, the most by any player since Michael Jordan dropped 303 in 1988-89. The only man who ever scored more through eight games was Wilt Chamberlain, who did it three times, peaking at a cartoonish 418 in 1962-63. Dončić is now keeping company that requires a museum membership. But the points are almost the least interesting thing about him. What makes him a problem without a solution is the tempo — the way he plays basketball at a speed that exists only inside his own nervous system, then drags the entire defense into that dimension whether they consent or not. He confounds defenses. You attempt to double-team him; that doesn't work. You attempt to play him one-on-one; he torches you. There is no gameplan to corral him; there is no player capable of stopping him. Watch what Dončić does to a defense, and you start to understand the quagmire. He lulls you. He pauses mid-dribble like a man checking his watch, lets you relax, then pulls the step-back before your nervous system registers the threat. He accelerates when you're flat-footed, brakes when you're sprinting, and punishes both. item.title: Beniers buries OT winner, Daccord gets his swagger back as Kraken top Flames
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Seattle Kraken bounced back Wednesday night after a four-goal loss to Calgary Oct. 30 to earn a 2-1 overtime win. Center Berkly Catton answered Flames forward Yegor Sharangovich’s first-period goal with Seattle’s only regulation goal, with 6:51 left, to force overtime. Matty Beniers scored in overtime to secure a win in the debut of the Kraken’s Hometown Remix jerseys. It was a win by committee, and a fitting end to the season series with the Flames. The American also opined that Andreeva’s coach, Conchita Martinez, encourages the youngster’s “diva” behavior on court. “Conchita’s always been very nice to me, but I lost a little respect for her, because I’m just like, this girl, she’s a nice girl. She’s a diva. She needs to be humbled. Conchita eggs on her behavior.” The 32-year-old went on to claim that, were Andreeva to adopt Gauff’s mentality, she would become a much better player overall than the former No. 2 and two-time Major singles champion: “It’s so funny cause if you see her and Coco’s mentality, if she had Coco’s mentality she’s better than her. item.title: Niko Kovac sets 17-point-target after latest Borussia Dortmund Champions League win
item.description: Niko Kovac sets 17-point-target after latest Borussia Dortmund Champions League win Borussia Dortmund moved onto nine points after four Champions League league-phase matches with a 2-1 victory over Real Betis on Wednesday night. Fabio Silva and Konstantinos Karetsas scored for Niko Kovac’s side as BVB registered their third win in four European matches and strengthened their position in the race for a top-eight finish. Speaking to DAZN after the game, Kovac highlighted the difficulty Dortmund faced against an experienced Betis side. “We created some promising plays after finding Julian Ryerson out wide. Betis was very compact in its four-three-three formation. It was obvious to everyone that this isn’t a team that accidentally stumbled into playing in the Champions League, but one that takes the field with very good, experienced players.” Kovac sets 17-to-18-point target for Borussia Dortmund Dortmund improved after the break, with Kovac satisfied that his side eventually earned a deserved victory. “In the second half, we played much better. We had to work hard, but the win is well-deserved and important for us. To finish in the top eight, we need seventeen or eighteen points. Now, we’ll see what happens when we go to London.” Kovac’s assessment leaves Dortmund needing another eight or nine points from their remaining four league-phase fixtures if his projected threshold proves accurate. Their next European test comes away against Arsenal after the international break before Inter visit Dortmund in December. BVB will be keen to avoid a repeat of last season’s late league-phase fade. Dortmund had collected 10 points from their opening five matches before taking only one point from their final three fixtures. A 2-2 draw with Bodø/Glimt was followed by defeats to Tottenham Hotspur and Inter, leaving Dortmund outside the top eight and forcing them into the knockout play-offs. With nine points already on the board this season, Kovac’s side have again placed themselves in a strong early position. item.title: Rare 'Bejeweled Brady' card found in hobby box
item.description: A $29.99 box of football cards has led two Jewett City brothers to a one-of-a-kind Tom Brady collectible that could bring hundreds of thousands of dollars at auction. Lucas, 23, and his younger brother Trevor, 18, discovered the rare “Bejeweled Brady” Garbage Pail Kids Superfractor, according to a community announcement. The card is a one-of-one collectible, meaning no other copy exists, and the estimated odds of pulling it from a standard hobby pack are approximately 1 in 10.5 million. Lucas had been collecting sports cards for only a little more than a month when he made the discovery. Weeks earlier, the brothers visited The Treasure Chest of Mystic, a newly opened collectibles store in Olde Mistick Village. They bought mystery autographed jersey boxes and found jerseys signed by Lawrence Taylor and LaMelo Ball. Store owner Carmine Lorusso photographed them celebrating the finds and shared the moment on the store's Facebook page. After finding the Brady card, the brothers returned to Lorusso for help. He assisted them with valuation, authentication, insurance and negotiations with auction houses, according to the announcement. Why the Tom Brady card could be so valuable Topps introduced Garbage Pail Kids in 1985, and the cartoon collectibles became a pop-culture phenomenon. The company has since brought the brand's artwork into sports cards featuring star athletes. The one-of-one Brady card brings together Garbage Pail Kids and a seven-time Super Bowl champion. A comparable sale provides a glimpse at the potential market. A one-of-one Garbage Pail Kids Superfractor featuring Cooper Flagg sold through Fanatics Collect for $288,000 on Aug. 28, according to the announcement. Fanatics Collect deal includes an advance Lorusso worked with Clay Thomas of Fanatics Collect to secure a guaranteed advance for Lucas before the Brady card goes to auction. Thomas was also involved in bringing the $288,000 Cooper Flagg Garbage Pail Kids card and a $8.04 million Cooper Flagg autographed rookie card to auction, according to the announcement. Fanatics offers advances of up to 50% of a card's minimum assessed value, according to the announcement. The advance provided for the Brady card therefore indicates a minimum assessed value of at least $150,000. Lucas is also set to receive 115% of the final winning bid under the negotiated payout agreement, representing the sale price plus 75% of the auction house's 20% buyer's premium, according to the announcement. The card was shipped to Thomas in Los Angeles with $350,000 in insurance coverage. item.description: Andoni Iraola reveals the ‘main reason’ why Liverpool lost to Fenerbahce Liverpool 2-3 Fenerbahce: Set-Piece Errors End Perfect Champions League Start Liverpool’s 100 per cent start in the Champions League is over, and there is no need to overcomplicate why. They were beaten 3-2 by Fenerbahce because they failed at the basics. Three set-pieces, three concessions, three warnings ignored. Andoni Iraola rotated after the weekend loss to Arsenal, making five changes and giving Bradley Barcola the central attacking role from the start. For a while, it looked sensible. Liverpool began well, moved the ball with purpose and went ahead through Trey Nyoni, whose volley took a deflection off Kojo Peprah Oppong and wrong-footed Ederson. It was Nyoni’s first senior goal for the club and a deserved reward for an energetic opening. Then came the sloppiness. Fenerbahce levelled through Mason Greenwood, his free-kick clipping Jeremy Jacquet on its way past Alisson. Another set-piece, another avoidable moment, another reminder that control means very little if you switch off when the ball stops moving. Photo: IMAGO Champions League control thrown away Liverpool still had enough quality to reclaim the lead. Iraola sent on Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo after the break, and the impact was immediate. Gakpo and Isak combined neatly, and the Sweden forward headed home to make it 2-1. At that point, Liverpool had the game where they wanted it. They did not keep it there. Four minutes later, Archie Brown restored parity for Fenerbahce, reacting sharply after pressure from another dead-ball situation. Late on, Vedat Muriqi completed the turnaround, rising to head in Brown’s delivery. Three Liverpool defenders were nearby, none dealt with it. That is the part Iraola will focus on, because he already said as much. “The main reason I can find to lose the game is we conceded [from] three set-pieces. It’s something that we were doing very well in the league, I think we were dealing [with it] quite well until today. “We knew it was one of the strengths of Fenerbahce but we concede from a free-kick, from a corner, even from the long throw at the end. “They are goals that have hurt us because we have twice gone in front after having good moments, controlling the game, arriving. “We found the goals. But after, we conceded in situations that we definitely should defend better. It’s frustration, because it’s a difficult place to come here and to play and we were for the most part of the game thinking, ‘OK, we can win this one.’ “But obviously it hasn’t happened. We have conceded, especially the first goal and the third goal – the second one is a rebound – but the wall, I don’t think we set it properly and the last one Muriqi jumps and wins the ball against three of our defenders, it’s something that definitely we have to defend better.” Fenerbahce comeback leaves Liverpool with work to do There is context here. item.description: Premier League Giants Circle For Russian Star Man Utd Track Aleksey Batrakov as Premier League Scouting Battle Intensifies Manchester United’s recruitment has too often felt like a contest between urgency and clarity, a search for immediate repair conducted at the expense of long-term design. That is why this latest development, credit to TEAMtalk , carries a certain intrigue. United were among the clubs represented in Istanbul this week as scouting interest gathered around Galatasaray’s Aleksey Batrakov, a 21-year-old attacking midfielder whose rise is beginning to draw in much of Europe’s elite. Arsenal and Chelsea were also present, which is instructive in itself. When clubs with different needs, different tactical ideas and different timelines all converge on the same player, it tends to suggest there is something a little more substantial at work than a passing trend. Batrakov has become one of those names, a talent moving beyond niche admiration and into the mainstream of elite recruitment. His numbers explain some of that fascination. Five goals and three assists in nine starts for Galatasaray is the sort of return that demands attention, especially for a player still settling into a new league after arriving from Lokomotiv Moscow in the summer. His performance against Stuttgart only deepened that impression, with two goals in a 2-0 win serving as another indication that he is comfortable occupying the decisive moments of high-level matches. Aleksey Batrakov Offers Creative Variety What makes Batrakov particularly compelling for Manchester United is not simply output, but profile. He is described primarily as a No 10, though the appeal appears to lie in his flexibility. He can drift wide, receive between the lines and contribute to the sort of fluid attacking structures that modern elite sides increasingly demand. In an age when specialists still matter but positional rigidity does not, that kind of adaptability can make a player highly marketable. United, Chelsea and Arsenal have all been linked before, and the sense now is that the circle of interest is widening further. Liverpool, Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur have all been credited with admiration, while Bayern Munich, RB Leipzig and Paris Saint-Germain are also said to be monitoring him. Once a market becomes this crowded, signing the player ceases to be only a football question. It becomes a test of conviction, timing and persuasion. item.description: Motorsport photo After Kimi Antonelli earned his maiden Formula 1 world title at the Mexico Grand Prix, Mercedes can add a ninth constructors’ trophy to its record in Brazil. The Silver Arrows have won 12 out of 19 grands prix so far this season, meaning they comfortably lead the championship. Only Ferrari can mathematically catch them, but that’s a tall order with a 126-point deficit. Mercedes had a first opportunity to triumph in Mexico, but that required a 1-2 and for Ferrari to score no more than four points. This time, the gap means the Brackley-based outfit just needs to outscore the Scuderia by at least three points in Sao Paulo. Non-exhaustive ways Mercedes can win the title at the Brazil GP Both Mercedes cars finish in the points and ahead of the Ferraris Mercedes takes a 1-2, 1-3 or 1-4 Mercedes finishes 2-3 or 2-4 and Ferrari doesn’t win Both Mercedes cars finish in the top five, no Ferrari on the podium Antonelli or Russell finishes in the top eight, both Ferraris retire Across the opening 19 rounds of the season (discounting sprint races), Mercedes has outscored Ferrari by three points or more on 10 occasions. Antonelli taking over from Hamilton as Mercedes’ hero Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes The 2026 season marks the first time Mercedes has won world titles without Lewis Hamilton since 1955, with the youthful Antonelli stepping up. “The championships with Lewis were absolutely incredible and rewarding,” team principal Toto Wolff said. “I felt that we all were part of Lewis' history, of the greatest champion, and that we would look back many years to come and say, ‘We've been world champions with Lewis Hamilton’. And this is something I'm very much still thinking about. item.description: Manchester United v AS Roma - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has suggested that pressures from beyond the dressing room have played a significant role in the club's disastrous start to the current campaign. Despite a morale-boosting victory in Europe, the Portuguese midfielder admitted that the environment surrounding Old Trafford has made life difficult for the players on the pitch. External pressures weighing on Old Trafford The Red Devils finally ended a dismal nine-match winless streak across all competitions with a dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday. However, the result does little to mask their domestic crisis, with Michael Carrick's side languishing in 17th place in the Premier League table. Speaking after the European triumph, Fernandes highlighted the mental toll that the club's current situation is taking on the first-team squad. "It’s a question of confidence," Fernandes explained during a candid post-match conversation with TNT Sport Brazil , as quoted by Manchester Evening News . "At this club, it’s difficult when results are negative. There are a lot of factors outside the dressing room, outside of the players and the backroom staff, which make the performances of the club and what we can do on the pitch more difficult. It affects a lot of players. Some deal with it better, some worse. We set high expectations for ourselves, and when things don’t work out, we end up mentally crushed by the frustration of not being able to give the club what we believe we’re truly capable of." A long-term cycle of disappointment Fernandes was quick to point out that these struggles are not a recent phenomenon but part of a wider trend that has plagued the record English champions for several seasons. The lack of silverware and consistent form has created an atmosphere where failure feels almost systemic, despite the high caliber of players currently residing in the home dressing room at Old Trafford. "When the situation is like this, there isn’t just one problem. There is more than one. There are a lot of things to improve, to do in a different way. Unfortunately for us, it’s been happening for a long time, which makes things more difficult. We know that no one at this club [likes to] not be winning. When you sign for this club, represent this club, it’s because you want something more. Unfortunately, it hasn’t been the case in the last few years," he said. item.description: It’s 10 miles from Northeast Washington, D.C., to Maryland ’s campus. For Aazaar Abdul-Rahim , it took a lifetime to cross that bridge. “Some people,” Abdul-Rahim told USA TODAY Sports, “call that on the opposite side of the bridge. That’s east of the river.” One of seven brothers raised in D.C., Abdul-Rahim grew up around Anacostia and the bridges that connect the city to everything beyond it. Now Maryland has asked him to build one of his own. WHAT'S NEXT? Maryland football has ambitious coaching targets. Here’s the reality The Terps’ interim coach must carry a struggling football program from the end of the Mike Locksley era toward an uncertain future. And Maryland has entrusted that job to someone who understands the place, its players and its pride as intimately as anyone. “A tremendous amount of pride, because I think this area is a unique area,” Abdul-Rahim said. “I’ve been all over the place, but this area is a unique area and a very prideful area. We march to our own beat here. We’re a little bit different than New York, and we’re a lot different than North Carolina. “We’re our own kind of separate entity, and I take pride in that.” Maryland football is a bit of a disjointed entity in an increasingly disjointed conference, where expansion has mandated 5,500-mile round trips to Big Ten “rival” Washington, along with similar treks to Oregon, UCLA and USC. Never the most-resourced program in the ultra-wealthy Big Ten, Maryland has nosedived to a 10-22 record since the start of the 2024 season. Little of that, though, traces to Abdul-Rahim’s impact. He arrived from a top defensive assistant role at Boston College and quickly helped the Terps lead the Big Ten in interceptions. His debut as interim head coach saw Maryland and favored Illinois combine for nearly 130 plays on SECU Stadium’s synthetic grass. The Terps lost on the very last one. They committed just one penalty and one turnover. They possessed the ball longer than Illinois.
